text.p: Italian Mario Cipollini snatched a second successive Tour de France stage victory on Monday.
The undisputed king of sprints surged in the last 20 metres of the longest stage -- 262 km from St Valery-de-Caux to Vire -- to retain race leadership.
Cipollini's sixth stage win in five Tours was one of his most impressive as he appeared to have been blocked in on the fence with only 100 metres left.
But he powered his way to the middle of the road to edge out German Erik Zabel, first in action on the final stretch, and another sprint ace, Dutchman Jeroen Blijlevens.
"It was a dangerous sprint but it was great. I had the luck and I also had the legs," said Cipollini, who also leads the points standings.
Winner of five stages in the recent Giro d'Italia, "Super Mario" said it would be increasingly difficult to complete the hat-trick because his rivals will be out for revenge.
But even though he does not have a chance of bringing the yellow jersey back to Paris, being as slow in mountains as he is fast in the sprints, Cipollini could not hide his pleasure.
"To win a sprint like I did today is an unbelievable feeling. It's impossible to feel such a strong emotion in the mountains or in time trials," he said. "It is short but it is intense."
Local hero Thierry Gouvenou, whose father owns a cycle shop in the finish town of Vire, in Normandy, did his best to prevent a mass sprint.
The Frenchman broke away after 139 km and remained alone in the lead for nearly 110 km before being caught 40 km from home.
Italian Fabiano Fontanelli and even big names such as France's Laurent Jalabert and Dutchman Erik Breukink also tried their luck in the final section but failed to make a decisive break.
Cipollini holds a 36-second lead over prologue winner Chris Boardman of Britain before Tuesday's 217 km third stage from Vire to Plumelec.
